description_clean: Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seenRelay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.THE TEAM• ~160 people,  around half in engineering, product and data• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentationRelay delivers 400,000 parcels a day through people who don't work for us: van drivers who choose their own shifts, local shops that hold parcels, and couriers who take them to the door. We went from 3,000 parcels a day in London to 400,000 across the UK in under three years.Delivery companies have always bought capacity by guesswork. Book too few drivers and parcels wait; book too many and you pay for empty vans. Most carriers accept that waste as the price of being reliable. Relay is building a marketplace where it isn't. You can't schedule drivers. You can only design what's on offer, and measure what happens.Every part of our network runs on decisions. The next two years are about building the systems that make them well, and proving they do. Engineering and operational research build what you design.Marketplace HighlightsYou own decision-making, not the model: you decide what Marketplace changes on booking, matching and shifts, and recommend on pay. Our scientists' models and experiments feed your calls, and the squad lead acts on them.Drivers choose when to work. What makes a shift worth booking early, and how do you prove what works when a clean experiment isn't possible?Every booked shift is paid, used or not, and every unserved route means late parcels. Where should each area sit between the two, and what would let the network get there on its own?Local shops hold our parcels while running their own businesses. Where does the network need more of them, what should a shop be paid, and how would you see a closed shop coming?A whole area, not a slice: no playbook, and the result is on the street the next morning.Analytics at the front, not in support: the squad's roadmap follows the analysis, in a data team of about 30 across analytics, operational research and data science.The OpportunityAs a Senior Product Analyst, Marketplace at Relay, you'll:Decide which Marketplace problems are real and which only look real, before anyone builds a fix.Design how Marketplace decides: which signals count, and what good looks like for booking, matching and pay.Tell the squad lead what to change and what to stop, and get a decision.Build the thing that decides: data applications, monitors and alerts, not decks, using Claude and agents to ship your own tools.Go and look when the data and the street disagree: the sort centre, the van, the shop.Get the missing data built, and prove whether each change worked. In a year, Marketplace's booking and pay decisions run on a system you designed.We're looking for candidates who…Have owned the decisions a matching, pricing or incentive model fed, in a two-sided marketplace or gig platform, rather than building the model itself.Have seen their work acted on: a leader changed a plan, a team adopted your method, or engineers built what you asked for.Can trace why drivers or couriers stop booking or cancel, and can read the experiments behind a pricing or incentive change, including when a clean test isn't possible.Have been through real change, such as a pivot, fast growth or a new market, and rebuilt something because of it.Are hands-on and fluent in SQL, with or without AI, and happy to build their own analysis apps, monitors and alerts.Would rather ship a working answer this week than a perfect one next quarter. No logistics experience needed, just the appetite to learn a physical operation fast.Don't tick every box? If this problem excites you, we'd still love to hear from you.Who Thrives at Relay?Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously.Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.1% Better Every Day: You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.All In, All the Time: You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.People-Powered Greatness: You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success.Grow the Whole Pie: You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect.Relay is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and fostering a workplace where everyone thrives.Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Stage : Construction automatique de modèles de processus hospitaliers multi- flux par grands modèles de langage (LLM)
description_clean: Projet porté par : Marwa Trabelsi - IMT Mines Albi Centre Génie Industriel (CGI) Partenaires IMT impliqués :Telecom Sud Paris, Département Electronique et Physique, Laboratoire Services répartis, Architectures,Modélisation, Validation, Administration des Réseaux (SAMOVAR): Nel Samama Mines Saint-Etienne : Centre Ingénierie Santé (CIS), Marius Huguet Sujet proposé (5-6 mois à partir de Février):Acronyme : HOPAL : Hospital Process Automatic LearningTitre long : Construction automatique de modèles de processus hospitaliers multi-flux par grands modèles de langage (LLM)Description du projet :L’étude du processus de prise en charge aux urgences est essentielle pour comprendre et résoudre le problème croissant de surcharge, qui touche de nombreux pays. Cette surcharge, souvent liée à un déséquilibre entre la demande de soins et les ressources disponibles, a des conséquences graves : retards de traitement, allongement des temps de triage, et même une augmentation de la mortalité. Elle révèle aussi des défis systémiques, comme l’accès difficile aux soins primaires, qui poussent les patients vers les urgences.Optimiser l’utilisation des ressources humaines et matérielles permet non seulement de réduire les files d’attente, mais aussi d’améliorer la qualité des soins et l’efficacité globale du système. Enfin, analyser ces processus aide à identifier des solutions durables, comme une meilleure organisation ou une réallocation ciblée des moyens.Ces processus laissent des traces numériques dans le système d'information hospitalier (SIH), mais leur modélisation reste aujourd'hui largement manuelle, coûteuse et rapidement obsolète.Le process mining permet de découvrir des modèles de processus à partir de ces traces. Les techniques classiques de découverte atteignent toutefois leurs limites face à des logs hétérogènes, bruités et multi-flux.Les grands modèles de langage (LLM) ouvrent une voie nouvelle : générer automatiquement des modèles de processus (BPMN, graphes de processus) directement à partir de traces organisationnelles, sans intervention humaine, et en produire une lecture compréhensible par les acteurs de terrain.Par ailleurs, des travaux menés au CGI ont démontré la faisabilité de la prédiction de parcours patients par LLM. La question scientifique au cœur de ce stage est l'articulation de ces deux briques : comment relier la prédiction de parcours à la construction automatique de modèles, pour passer de modèles rétrospectifs (ce qui s'est passé) à des modèles prospectifs (ce qui va se passer) ?Ce projet s’inscrit dans une dynamique inter-écoles IMT autour de l’IA explicable pour la santé publique. Les équipes CGI, CIS et SAMOVAR collaborent déjà via le projet TRACKING (Carnot M.I.N.E.S – CARINGS), avec des travaux sur la géolocalisation indoor au sein des urgences de l’Hôpital Le Corbusier de Firminy. Cette synergie s’est prolongée par un stage M2 en 2025, financé par le Fonds d’amorçage Santé, dédié au prototypage d’une application mobile de localisation indoor/outdoor des patients. Une thèse INTERCARNOT a été lancé dans la continuité avec la validation des deux instituts Carnot (M.I.N.E.S et TSN) et va démarrer en Octobre 2026.Objectif du stageL'objectif est de concevoir et prototyper un pipeline dans lequel un même module de construction automatique de modèles par LLM est alimenté par deux sources :Branche A (rétrospective) : les logs SIH réels, normalisés en event logs, produisent des modèles as-is des processus observés ;Branche B (prospective) : dans la suite des travaux réalisés, les parcours prédits par LLM sont sérialisés au même format de traces (activité, timestamp, ressource) via un adaptateur, et produisent des modèles to-be des processus à venir.La comparaison des modèles as-is et to-be permet la détection d'écarts, l'anticipation des goulots d'étranglement et le support à la décision explicable, jusqu'à la simulation contrefactuelle (perturber les prédictions, reconstruire le modèle, observer l'impact).Profil recherchéFormation : M2 ou dernière année d'école d'ingénieur en informatique, science des données, IA ou génie industriel ;Compétences techniques : Python indispensable ; une expérience des LLM (fine-tuning, prompting, API)et/ou du process mining (pm4py) est un atout fort ;Qualités : rigueur scientifique, autonomie, goût pour le travail avec des données réelles imparfaites, intérêt pour le domaine hospitalier.RéférencesHuguet M, Pehlivan C, Ballereau F, Dodane-Loyenet A, Fontanili F, Garaix T, Yordanov Y, Augusto V, Tazarourte K, Redjaline A. title: CENTRALE LYON - Postdoctoral Researcher Position Deep Learning for Functional-Oxide Growth Video-to-Spectrum Prediction by RHEED / XRD Fusion
description_clean: PROJECT OVERVIEW We are looking for a highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to develop innovative deeplearning models that predict the structure of functional-oxide thin films directly from their growth dynamics. Positioned at the interface between Artificial Intelligence and materials physics, the OXYD-IA project aims to design a deep model able to predict the final X-ray Diffraction (XRD) spectrum of an oxide thin film from the sole Reflection High-Energy Electron Diffraction (RHEED) video recorded during its growth by Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE). The resulting tool will open the way to predictive, in situ control of oxide epitaxy – a process today dominated by a costly trial-and-error approach, in which the structural and functional properties of the films are only validated ex situ. You will join a genuinely multidisciplinary collaboration between the INL (Institut des Nanotechnologies de Lyon), which provides the operando experimental data and materials-physics expertise, and the LIRIS (équipe Imagine), which provides the deep video-learning and probabilistic-modelling methodology – both at École Centrale de Lyon. A high-impact opportunity. AI for experimental physics is a fast-growing field, and OXYD-IA offers a genuine first-mover advantage within it: you would work on a unique, unpublished dataset of paired RHEED videos and XRD spectra to build one of the first video-to-spectrum models with calibrated uncertainty for oxide growth. By learning directly from experimental 1 data, such a model can short-circuit the traditional trial-and-error loop, accelerate discovery and drastically cut experimental time, cost, precursor consumption and instrument occupancy – turning routine in situ diagnostics into predictive tools. Scientific context. Epitaxial perovskite-oxide thin films exhibit rich, tunable functional properties (thermoelectricity, ferroelectricity, piezoelectricity) governed by their structure and composition, themselves correlated with the growth conditions. MBE offers independent control of each element but, applied to oxides, is notoriously unstable and poorly reproducible because of the oxidising atmosphere. RHEED tracks the surface dynamics in real time (lattice parameter, surface reconstructions, roughness) but does not give access to the final bulk microstructure, which is only reachable ex situ via XRD / XRR. There is therefore a strong physical link – so far unexploited quantitatively – between RHEED dynamics and final XRD microstructure, which OXYD-IA proposes to learn directly.Figure 1 – OXYD-IA pipeline. At inference, the RHEED video acquired during growth (INL) feeds a deep video encoder (LIRIS) and a probabilistic regression module that predicts the final XRD spectrum together with its uncertainty. During training, the predicted spectrum is compared with the ex situ XRD / XRR spectrum measured at INL (ground truth); this discrepancy is the supervised learning signal that adjusts the model parameters.KEY RESEARCH AREAS AND RESPONSIBILITIES You will drive the core computational research along a risk-managed, phased 12-month roadmap. The primary target is a versioned RHEED / XRD dataset, growth-regime classification and probabilistic regression of the key structural parameters with calibrated uncertainty; full-spectrum prediction, a real-time demonstrator and cross-oxide generalisation are stretch and follow-on objectives. The work is organised around three technical pillars: 1. Corpus structuring and spatio-temporal RHEED representation • Build a versioned dataset by cleaning, temporally aligning and pairing the RHEED video sequences, the associated MBE parameters (temperature, oxygen pressure, source fluxes) and the ex situ XRD / XRR spectra (SrTiO3 reference system). • Pre-train, in a self-supervised manner, a spatio-temporal video encoder (3D CNN, e.g. R(2+1)D, or temporal Vision Transformer) fine-tuned on the laboratory corpus. • Perform fuzzy / Bayesian classification of the growth regimes (2D vs. 3D modes, transitions, RHEED oscillations), building on LIRIS expertise in the statistical analysis of sequences. 2. Probabilistic RHEED →XRD regression with uncertainty quantification • Design a latent representation that couples the video encoding with the physical MBE parameters. • Learn stepwise – first scalar structural parameters (lattice parameter, density, mosaicity), more robust at small N, then the full 1D XRD spectrum. • Provide calibrated uncertainty estimates (Bayesian approaches or deep ensembles), indispensable for guiding real-time decisions during growth. 3. Real-time demonstrator and dissemination (stretch / follow-on) • Validate the model on new SrTiO3 growths and prototype an in-growth inference tool at the end of the NANOFUTUR MBE line. • Mitigate the small-data and generalisation challenges through temporal data augmentation, transfer learning from pre-trained video encoders and domain adaptation towards other functional oxides. • Contribute toward a high-impact joint publication at the AI / materials interface (the project milestone is the submission of a joint paper).  REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS • A Ph.D. in the field of Artificial Intelligence – Computer Science, Machine Learning, Computer Vision or Signal Processing, and we are looking for a senior postdoc with 2–5 years of post-PhD experience. • Deep learning on sequential / video data: demonstrable, hands-on experience with 3D CNNs, temporal transformers and / or probabilistic models. Proficiency in Python and PyTorch (or TensorFlow) is mandatory. • A genuine appetite for physics: a strong curiosity for, or prior exposure to, experimental physics and materials science. The ideal candidate carried out an AI-focused Ph.D. and is eager to apply it to a real materials-physics problem. • Research mindset: a track record of innovation and the ability to work autonomously on a complex, multidisciplinary project. • Software skills: experience with Git version control and reproducible research. • Excellent communication and scientific-writing skills in English. ADDITIONAL SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES • Self-supervised video pre-training, uncertainty quantification (Bayesian / ensembles), fuzzy classification, or domain adaptation. • Experience with small-sample / transfer-learning settings and handling large-scale experimental datasets.HOW TO APPLY Please prepare a single PDF file containing: 1. A detailed Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications. 2. A 1-page motivation letter explaining your specific interest in this project and how your background addresses the key responsibilities and qualifications listed above. 3. The names and contact information of at least two academic references. Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

title: Chief Information Security Officer
description_clean: Who We AreCatalyst Capital is a profitable, bootstrapped holding company building a diversified financial services group: education, publishing, software, wealth and tax planning tools, investment products and proprietary trading technology. Funded entirely from its own operating cash. We have never taken outside capital.The cash engine is Decentralized Masters, a DeFi education business that went from zero to 150+ people, 4,500+ paying members and roughly $48.6M of FY26 revenue at ~25% earnings before tax in four years. That engine funds everything else on this page.Role summaryCatalyst Capital is hiring its first Chief Information Security Officer to own security across every brand in the group. You will set the strategy, build the program, and personally run the response when something goes wrong.The job is two halves. Half is the core of a CISO's role: incident response, identity and access, vendor risk, phishing defense, policy and audit readiness, and the judgment calls only a person can own. The other half is making security AI-driven: mapping our full surface and building agentic systems that test, monitor and audit it with near-total coverage, so security keeps pace as more of the company runs on AI. This is a player-coach role: about half hands-on, leading a small team of engineers.You report to Group leadership, brief the leadership team monthly, and are the person they trust to explain risk in plain language and make the call under pressure.What you will ownCore security leadership (about half)Security strategy and program. Own the security strategy, roadmap and budget across Decentralized Masters, Legacy, Inflection Club, Sentinelis and future brands. Report posture, top risks and trends to leadership every month, with a risk register leadership can act on.Incident response. Own IR end to end: detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery and the postmortem. Lead the room during a live incident and coordinate with legal counsel, forensics firms, insurers and regulators. Keep runbooks current and run tabletop exercises.Cloud and identity security. Own identity and access across the group: SSO, MFA, least-privilege roles, admin redundancy and short-lived credentials. Set the AWS security baseline.Third-party and vendor risk. Assess the security of every vendor and data provider we depend on, including their audits and attestations, and set the bar a vendor must clear before connecting to our systems or data.Platform and customer account security. Set the standards for login protection and account-takeover defense on our platforms, and work with the engineering teams that own each platform to build them in.Phishing and impersonation defense. Own email security, staff training and phishing simulations. Run brand protection: find and take down fake domains and accounts impersonating our brands and leaders.Policy, compliance and trust. Write and enforce policies people actually follow. Prepare the company for SOC 2 or ISO 27001 with Legal & Compliance. Own the public security and trust story, including the trust page on our products.Team leadership. Manage and develop our security engineers, decide what we build in-house versus outsource, and grow the team only where automation cannot do the job.Member scam awareness. Supply the security content behind scam-awareness messaging to members, working with Community, Support and Marketing. Legal approves the wording.AI-driven security (about half)Full attack-surface map. Build and maintain a living inventory of everything we run: internal apps, cloud, code repos, and every SaaS tool and integration (CRM, telephony, community, payments, data providers). Know what connects to what, who has access, and what is logged.Agentic security harness. Design and run AI-driven systems that approach 100% coverage: automated code and dependency review, continuous configuration and access audits, and vendor documentation review. Humans set direction and make the judgment calls; agents do the exhaustive work.AI-driven detection and logging. Own the security stack (SIEM, Rapid7; endpoint protection; email security; identity and device management), make sure every critical system sends usable logs, and use AI to triage alerts and hunt across them.Secure AI and vibe-coding standards. Set the rules for how teams build with AI: what can ship, what data AI tools may touch, and the review path before anything with customer data goes live.AI agent security. As more of the company runs on agents and automations, secure them: scoped credentials and tool permissions, prompt-injection defense, data exposure, and monitoring and guardrails for agents in production. Required Experience and SkillsExtensive hands-on experience with IBM z/OS and Mainframe technologies.Strong background in z/OS system programming or mainframe infrastructure.Broad knowledge of mainframe technologies and enterprise environments.Previous experience in technical training, workshops or mentoring.Excellent communication and presentation skills.Ability to deliver engaging training sessions in English.Program DetailsKick-off event: 11 January 2027 – on-site in Stockholm, SwedenTraining period: 8 February – 30 April 2027Workload: Full-time engagement during the training periodLocation: Primarily remote, with selected on-site days in Stockholm, SwedenLanguage: EnglishPreparation: Dedicated and remunerated preparation time will be scheduled in addition to the training days, allowing sufficient time to develop training materials, prepare exercises and set up practical learning activities.If you have extensive IBM z/OS experience and enjoy teaching and mentoring the next generation of Mainframe professionals, we would be delighted to hear from you.Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Project Manager BESS (m/w/d)
description_clean: Wir sind ein mittelständisches Familienunternehmen mit 500 Mitarbeitenden an verschiedenen Standorten in Deutschland. Als Ingenieurs- und Beratungsdienstleister sind wir weltweit in Projekten tätig, welche die Energiewende vorantreiben, den Schutz der Umwelt fördern und zur Verbesserung unser aller Lebensqualität beitragen.Als Senior Project Manager BESS /m/w/d) übernehmen Sie die Verantwortung für anspruchsvolle Batteriespeicherprojekte in Deutschland und begleiten diese von der Planung bis zur erfolgreichen Inbetriebnahme. Zur Vertstärkung unseres Teams suchen wir engagierte Persönlichkeiten an verschiedenen Standorten deutschlandweit, die mir ihrer Expertise den Ausbau moderner Energiespeicherlösungen vorantreiben möchten.Aufgaben, die motivieren:Projektmanagement von BESS-Projekten (Battery Energy Storage Systems) mit Schwerpunkt auf dem deutschen MarktErfahrung mit den deutschen Genehmigungsanforderungen (z. B. BImSchG/BImSchV)Unterstützung der Beschaffung sowie Leitung von Ausschreibungs- und VergabeverfahrenUnterstützung während der Bau- und InbetriebnahmephaseKoordination von Nachunternehmern sowie Sicherstellung von QA/QC (Qualitätssicherung und Qualitätskontrolle)Unterstützung des Vertriebsteams bei der Akquise neuer ProjekteQualifikationen, die überzeugen:Abgeschlossenes Studium im Bereich Erneuerbare Energien, Elektrotechnik, Energietechnik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung6–8 Jahre Berufserfahrung im Bereich elektrotechnischer Anlagen in DeutschlandErfahrung in der Planung von Anlagen im Bereich der erneuerbaren Energien, Batteriespeichersystemen (BESS) oder anderen elektrotechnischen Anlagen in DeutschlandDeutsch-, und Englischkenntnisse auf C1 NiveauReisebreitschaftFührerschein  notwendigWorüber wir uns freuen: Wenn Sie für Ihren Job brennen, egal welcher ethnischen Herkunft, Religion oder Weltanschauung Sie angehören. Auch Geschlecht, Behinderung, Alter oder sexuelle Identität spielen für uns keine Rolle. Hauptsache, Sie passen zu uns!  91% unserer Mitarbeitenden stimmen der Aussage zu, dass ILF in Deutschland ein "Great Place to work" ist:Sympathische Unternehmenskultur und gelebte VIeLFalt: Viele lokale aber auch überregionale Live-Events prägen unser Miteinander und der Großteil der Mitarbeitenden ist per "Du". Besonders stolz macht uns die Internationalität unseres Teams mit mehr als 30 unterschiedlichen Nationen.Moderne Arbeitsumgebung: An allen Standorten sind unsere Arbeitsplätze technisch hochwertig und mit höhenverstellbaren Schreibtischen ausgestattet. Auch wenn es uns von anderen Unternehmen vielleicht nicht unterscheidet: Wir bieten freie Getränke, den obligatorischen Obstkorb und weitere Snacks für Zwischendurch inklusive Eis im Sommer.Entwicklung und Netzwerken: Wir planen für alle Mitarbeitenden jährliche Weiterbildungsbudgets ein, die für externe Angebote (z.B. Udemy) und unsere interne ILF-Academy genutzt werden können. Außerdem wird in regelmäßigen Feedbackgesprächen auf Wunsch die Möglichkeit neuer oder erweiterter Verantwortungsbereiche besprochen. Gleitzeitkonto und verschiedene Teilzeitvarianten) und Arbeitsort (z.B. mobiles Arbeiten, Standortwechsel, Auslandseinsätze). As a Product Designer at 360Learning, you will work embedded in a product squad while being a full member of the Product Design team under the governance of the Head of Product Design.
You will join the e-Learning Experience (ELXP) squad, whose mission is to Empower any user to create high-quality and interactive content effortlessly, with AI support.
In this role, you will collaborate daily with Product Managers and Engineers to solve complex product problems end-to-end. You will translate product vision, user insights, and technical constraints into intuitive, scalable, and consistent experiences. Beyond your squad, you will actively contribute to design excellence across the product by participating in shared standards, rituals, and continuous improvement of craft and quality.
This role is designed for a Confirmed Product Designer looking to deepen their impact on a complex B2B product.
What You'll DoWithin 1 month

Onboard into your product squad, the Product Design team, and key cross-functional partners
Understand 360Learning’s product vision, Authoring strategy, and Convexity culture
Get familiar with our tools, design system, and product development processes
Start contributing to your first design initiatives
Participate actively in design critiques and product rituals

Within 3 months

Be a reliable and proactive contributor within your squad
Design and iterate on complex user flows related to content creation, collaboration, and AI-supported features
Conduct or support user research and use insights and data to inform design decisions
Deliver high-quality design solutions from discovery to handoff
Ensure consistency and usability across your scope in alignment with shared design standards
Actively participate in cross-squad design rituals to help raise the overall quality bar

Within 6 months

Own significant parts of the Authoring experience with increasing autonomy
Lead design discussions and workshops with Product Managers, Engineers, and other stakeholders
Contribute to improving design and collaboration processes within your squad
Participate in transversal initiatives such as the design system, accessibility, or shared UX patterns
Develop a solid understanding of 360Learning’s business model, market, and product constraints

Within 12 months

Be a strong reference designer on your scope while contributing to design excellence across the product
Help shape the long-term Authoring experience vision in close collaboration with your Product Manager
Advocate for user-centered design and clearly articulate its value and impact to non-design stakeholders
Support and mentor more junior designers when relevant
Continuously bring thoughtful improvements and innovation to the product

The Skill Set

4+ years of experience as a Product Designer on digital products, ideally in B2B SaaS
Ability to design complex workflows and systems while keeping experiences intuitive and usable
Product thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to balance user needs, business goals, and technical constraints
Experience working closely with Product Managers and Engineers in a squad model
High proficiency in Figma, including components, variants, and prototyping
Ability to own a scope from discovery to delivery with growing autonomy
Strong communication skills and ability to clearly explain design decisions
Willingness to contribute to shared design standards and collective design excellence
Fluent English (US/UK) / B2 level or equivalent (FR)
Enthusiasm for our working environment explained here:  https://bit.ly/Convexity_360L 

Nice to have...


Experience designing authoring tools, editors, or builder-style interfaces
Exposure to LMS platforms or enterprise standards such as SCORM or LTI
Experience or strong interest in AI-assisted or automation-driven product experiences
Knowledge of accessibility and inclusive design principles
Experience contributing to or evolving a design system


What We Offer

Compensation: Package includes base salary, a variable component and equity 📈
Benefits/Perks: Work From Home stipend, RTT, lunch vouchers, medical insurance, gym subscription, 1 month parental leave for the second parent. 
Balance: Flexible hours, full remote work possible anywhere in France 🏠. Working remotely from outside France is also possible, subject to some conditions (tenure, performance, destination, length, etc.) and the approval of our Remote Committee 🌍
Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion: We have 6 active ERGs including Mental Health, Environmental/Sustainability, Women, Parents, LGBTQIA2S+, and Ethnic Diversity. Each group has at least one executive team member serving as a member of the group, bringing greater awareness to each group’s activities and providing a quick path to impact 🤝

title: Chief Financial Officer
description_clean:
360Learning is entering its next phase of growth. Today, more than 2,500 organizations worldwide rely on us to turn internal expertise into business performance. As AI reshapes how companies develop skills and share knowledge, we are bringing together Collaborative Learning, AI and enterprise-grade infrastructure to redefine the future of L&D.
We are now looking for a Chief Financial Officer / VP Finance to help lead this next chapter.
Reporting directly to Benjamin Marchal, our CEO, you will lead our global Finance organization and act as a strategic partner to the CEO, Executive Committee and Board.
Your mission: drive sustainable, profitable growth while strengthening financial discipline, operational performance and long-term value creation. You will help shape our SaaS operating model, optimize resource allocation and balance growth, profitability and cash generation.
Working closely with leaders across Revenue, Product, People and Operations, you will turn financial insights into business decisions, foster accountability and support our strategic priorities, including M&A, investor relations and future liquidity events.
We are looking for a Finance leader who combines strategic vision, strong business judgment and hands-on execution. Whether you are an experienced CFO or a VP Finance ready to step up, this is an opportunity to work directly with the CEO and Board and shape some of the company's most consequential decisions.
Within 1 month, you will:


Understand 360Learning's strategy, financial performance, organization, culture and key business priorities.


Build strong relationships with the CEO, Executive Committee, Finance team and key internal stakeholders.


Review our financial reporting, forecasting, budgeting and performance management processes.


Assess the maturity of our Finance organization, systems, internal controls and financial governance.


Identify the main drivers of growth, profitability, cash generation and operational efficiency.


Deliver an initial diagnostic highlighting key risks, opportunities and short-term priorities.


Within 3 months, you will:


Build and align with the CEO on an 18-month Finance roadmap, covering financial performance, operational efficiency, systems, processes, governance and team development.


Strengthen financial visibility through accurate forecasting, clear SaaS metrics and actionable management reporting.


Establish a strong financial business partnering approach with Revenue, Product, People and other functions.


Identify opportunities to improve cost efficiency, productivity and resource allocation while protecting strategic investments.


Review our financial systems and data infrastructure, identifying automation and scalability opportunities.


Take ownership of Board reporting, investor communications and financial planning processes.


Assess our current M&A framework and identify opportunities to strengthen due diligence and post-acquisition performance tracking.


Within 12 months, you will:


Drive measurable progress towards our growth and profitability ambitions, improving financial efficiency, cash generation and Rule of 40 performance.


Establish a best-in-class financial operating model, with reliable forecasts, transparent KPIs and clear accountability across functions.


Lead strategic financial initiatives to optimize our cost structure, improve unit economics and support sustainable ARR growth.


Build a high-performing, scalable global Finance organization combining strategic business partnering with strong operational execution.


Strengthen financial governance, compliance, audit readiness and risk management across our international entities.


Support the evaluation, execution and financial integration of strategic acquisitions.


Partner with the CEO and Board on long-term financial strategy, capital structure and potential future fundraising or liquidity scenarios.


Make Finance a key driver of business performance and shareholder value creation.


The Skill Set:


10+ years in Finance, including senior leadership in B2B SaaS, ideally scaling from €30–50M to €100M+ ARR.


Strong grasp of ARR, NRR, CAC, LTV, gross margin, retention and Rule of 40.


Expertise in forecasting, financial modeling, performance management and data-driven decision-making.


Ability to balance growth investments, profitability, cash generation and operational efficiency.


Trusted advisor to the CEO and Executive Committee, able to challenge assumptions and drive accountability.


Experience with PE/Growth Equity investors, Board reporting, financial governance and capital allocation.


Exposure to M&A, due diligence, fundraising and capital structure; transaction leadership is a plus.


Strong command of accounting, reporting, treasury, cash management, compliance and internal controls.


Track record of building high-performing teams, automating processes and scaling international Finance operations.


Hands-on, pragmatic and accountable, aligned with Convexity’s values of Impact, Rational Thinking, High Accountability and Scalability. Fluent English; French is a plus.

Benefits/Perks: Work From Home stipend, RTT, lunch vouchers, medical insurance, gym subscription, 1 month parental leave for the second parent.


Balance: Flexible hours, full remote work possible anywhere in France 🏠

Each group has at least one executive team member serving as a member of the group, bringing greater awareness to each group’s activities and providing a quick path to impact 🤝

title: Forward Deployed Engineer – SAP (m/f/d)
description_clean: About QoreloAlmost every company running SAP faces the same task: the move to SAP S/4HANA. These programmes run for years, cost tens of millions, and regularly stall at the same point. Nobody fully understands the legacy landscape that has grown over decades.That is where Qorelo comes in. We are building the AI platform for S/4HANA transformation. Qorelo reads code, processes, documentation and how the system is actually used, makes the existing landscape transparent, and delivers the fit-to-standard analysis in weeks instead of months. We take a clean core, target-architecture-first approach and carry it end to end across SAP Activate, from Discover to Realize. The knowledge stays with the customer afterwards, long after the system integrators have moved on.We have raised $3.5M from HPI Ventures, the fund tied to the institute of SAP co-founder Hasso Plattner, along with other strong backers. We already work with Fortune 500 and DAX 40 companies, including Mercedes-Benz.The roleAs a Forward Deployed Engineer, you are Qorelo’s technical face at the customer. You run workshops and demos on the customer’s real SAP landscape, get Qorelo connected to their systems and tools, and make sure the platform delivers on their data and their processes. Then you bring what you learned back to our engineers.You work directly with our engineering team and solution architects, report to Marino, our CTO, and spend a real share of your time with customers, both on site and remotely.What you will ownSAP connectivity. RFC connections, technical users and authorisations. You make the connection work and explain it to Basis and security teams in their language.Workshops and demos on real environments. You run on-site workshops of several hours and show Qorelo on the customer’s own SAP landscape, not a sandbox: their custom code, their processes, their data. You prepare together with sales and our solution architects, and you handle the technical questions in the room.Integrations. You connect the customer’s tools to Qorelo through our existing integrations across the SAP, Atlassian, Microsoft and similar ecosystems, and make sure they work on the customer’s landscape.The feedback loop. What you see at customers (where the product wins, where it falls short, what they asked for) comes back to engineering and product as clear, concrete feedback. You are the engineering team’s eyes and ears at the customer.What you need5+ years in technical, customer-facing roles around SAP: technical SAP consultant, solutions or presales engineer, or an engineer who spent much of their time with customers.Solid SAP technical understanding: you know how an SAP landscape fits together (ECC, S/4HANA), what RFC connections, technical users and authorisations are, and what a Basis team will ask you. You do not need to be an ABAP developer.Enough technical depth to set up and troubleshoot a connection with the customer’s IT: credentials, firewalls, proxies, VPN, certificates.Strong presence in the room: you can run a five-hour workshop with consultants, IT leads and process owners, demo live on their system, and keep it on track when something does not work.Real AI curiosity: you use LLM tools yourself and can explain clearly what Qorelo does and where its limits are.Willingness to travel within Europe for on-site demos and workshops.Fluent English. Meaningful equity and a direct hand in how Qorelo runs in the field. We are looking for people who want to shape a company, not join one.Competitive salary, benchmarked for senior customer-facing technical talent in Berlin.The problems. Fortune 500 and DAX 40 production landscapes, including Mercedes-Benz. You work at the core of SAP systems most engineers never get to touch.The team. Short paths, fast decisions, and a direct line to our CTO, our founding engineer and our solution architects.25 days paid vacation + German public holidays.Company offsites with the whole team.An office at the Wasserturm in Prenzlauer Berg – where you work when you are not with customers. title: Sr. Software Engineer, Cloud Platform
description_clean:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.About the role:
As a Senior Engineer in the Infrastructure org, you will help evolve the cloud foundations behind every Samsara product. Your goal will be to reduce systemic production risk and enable continued growth by making infrastructure safer to change, easier to operate, and more resilient and cost-efficient at scale.
You will bring deep expertise in at least one infrastructure domain, such as compute and workload orchestration, networking, storage and stateful systems, or cloud control planes, and apply it across our multi-account, multi-region AWS environment. You will lead work such as modernizing compute and stateful infrastructure, strengthening capacity and failure isolation, and building standardized infrastructure-as-code workflows and reusable automation.
You will partner with product engineering teams to turn recurring risks and manual operations into durable platforms and paved paths. We do not expect you to be an expert in every infrastructure domain. We are looking for engineers who have built and operated critical systems at significant scale, understand how infrastructure fails, and can use that experience to improve both our platforms and our engineering practices.
You should apply if:

You want to impact the industries that run our world: The software, firmware, and hardware you build will result in real-world impact, helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are a life-long learner: We have ambitious goals. Every Samsarian has a growth mindset as we work with a wide range of technologies, challenges, and customers that push us to learn on the go.
You believe customers are more than a number: Samsara engineers enjoy a rare closeness to the end user and you will have the opportunity to participate in customer interviews, collaborate with customer success and product managers, and use metrics to ensure our work is translating into better customer outcomes.
You are a team player: Working on our Samsara Engineering teams requires a mix of independent effort and collaboration. Motivated by our mission, we're all racing toward our connected operations vision, and we intend to win together.

In this role, you will: 

Design, build, and operate reliable cloud platforms, bringing depth in one or more areas such as compute, networking, storage, stateful systems, or infrastructure control planes.
Improve the scalability, capacity management, isolation, recovery, and cost efficiency of critical production infrastructure.
Build standardized infrastructure-as-code workflows and reusable automation that support self-service provisioning, testing, progressive rollout, reconciliation, rollback, and drift prevention. 
Identify shared failure modes and build safeguards that prevent localized failures from escalating into broad customer impact.
Contribute to multi-account, multi-region, and isolated AWS architectures, including regulated environments such as GovCloud.
Participate in operational ownership and incident response, using incidents and near misses to drive durable architectural improvements.
Mentor engineers, raise the quality of infrastructure design and operational judgment, and establish patterns that can be adopted across the organization.
Clearly communicate architecture, trade-offs, risks, and migration plans to technical and organizational stakeholders.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

Minimum requirements for this role.

6+ years of experience designing and building software, infrastructure, or distributed systems, including operating critical systems in production.
Deep expertise in at least one of the following: compute and workload orchestration, networking, storage and stateful systems, or cloud infrastructure control planes.
Strong software-engineering fundamentals in Go, Python, Java, or a similar language.
Hands-on experience designing and operating infrastructure on a major public cloud platform; AWS experience is preferred.
Experience using infrastructure as code, such as Terraform, to safely manage production infrastructure.
Strong understanding of capacity management, failure domains, observability, rollout safety, and production recovery.
Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical initiatives across teams and through ambiguous problem spaces.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience

An ideal candidate also has:

Designing and operating large-scale compute or container platforms such as ECS, EKS, Kubernetes, or similar orchestration systems.
Designing and operating stateful distributed systems such as Kafka, OpenSearch, managed databases, caching, or large-scale storage platforms.
Building internal infrastructure platforms, control planes, or self-service developer experiences adopted across multiple teams.
Designing multi-account or multi-region cloud architectures with strong workload isolation and disaster recovery.
Leading major infrastructure migrations while maintaining availability and controlling operational risk.
Delivering measurable improvements in infrastructure capacity, cost efficiency, or developer self-service.

lasting fixes.Balance near-term pipeline fixes with foundational investments, and make clear tradeoffs in a fast-moving environment.Stay hands-on where it matters: review designs, help debug tough ability to work independently with minimal guidance, proactively manages tasks and priorities across multiple projects, analyzes and executes work efficiently, collaborates effectively with title: Product Engineering Lead
description_clean: Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zoneHi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.That means a top-notch engineer who leads from the codebase. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You'll ship every week and lead the team's biggest technical work — and as the team grows, you'll grow into managing it.You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.— GrigoryWhy Secfix existsOver 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.What you'll actually do in the first 3 monthsThis isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. By the end of the month, the team should be bringing you their hardest technical questions — because you've earned it, not because of the title.Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start pairing and doing technical 1:1s with two or three engineers, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.Month 3: Own technical hiring. Take over the technical interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?After the first quarter, the job is the technical decisions — and, as the team grows, management. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — you'll run the technical side of it.Most of your time stays in the code: you ship every week and own the specs, architecture, and reviews on our biggest projects. As the team grows, you'll take on 1:1s, growth conversations, and eventually managing the team.Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.Team and hiring. Technical interviews and mentoring now; 1:1s, growth conversations, and the EM role as we grow.AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff.What success looks likeAt 6 months: You've led at least 2-3 major projects from spec to production. The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality.At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've taken over 1:1s as the team grew, and you're ready to step into the EM role.How we workWe've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture.Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture; give it a read.To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year:Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution.AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it here.Zero-bugs. We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. Critical issues get fixed immediately. High-severity within 48 hours. Every bug has an owner. Weekly quality review as part of Monday planning. Quality as identity, in compliance, being correct isn't a nice-to-have; it's the entire value proposition. We care about edge cases, data integrity, and getting the details right. Customers notice the speed and polish before they can name it. That kind of quality builds trust. In our category, trust is the product.We build what customers need, not what they ask for. Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us.This role is for you if:You've led a team technically and made it ship faster. You've set its technical direction, run its design reviews, and interviewed for it — and you can point to where cycle time dropped because of you.You know what great engineers look like. You've thought deeply about what makes them productive, what holds them back, and how to move them forward — and you can spot one in a single interview.You have an exceptional IC track record. You're a senior or staff engineer whose code and designs others build on — and you want to grow into managing, not escape coding.You have product taste. You notice when a feature ships on time but isn't good enough, and you say so.You hold people to a high standard. You're comfortable giving direct feedback and having hard conversations in code reviews and design discussions.You're hands-on with AI-assisted development. You've used Cursor and Claude Code in real production work, not just toy projects. You have opinions about how AI changes the engineering workflow from ideation to release, and you want to push a team to keep getting faster.You've worked in startups. You know what it feels like when there's low process, and the answer is "figure it out and ship it."You think engineering culture can stay startup-like at scale. You're optimistic that a small, high-performing team can stay that way as it grows, with little process.You communicate proactively in writing. In a remote team, written communication is how decisions get made and context gets shared. But you're not scared of jumping into a pair programming session either.What we're looking forRequired8+ years as a software engineer at senior or staff level, including 1+ years as a tech lead (formal or de facto) for a team of 3+You've shipped AI features to production — retrieval, RAG, agentic workflows — and you know the difference between a demo that works and one that holds up on real customer dataProduct taste: a keen sense for what makes a product feel great, and the habit of saying so when it doesn'tYou've built and shipped with Claude Code and Cursor in real production work, and you have opinions about where AI helps and where it quietly creates debtYou lead system design, not just contribute to it: you write the spec, own the architecture, and drive it to productionStrong OOP fundamentals; Java Spring Boot, Hibernate, or equivalentRelational database design and SQL optimisationExperience interviewing engineering candidatesYou've built something zero to one at a startup, or scaled a team through the messy middle. You know what it feels like when there's no playbookAble to work in European timezone (CET/CEST). EMEA-based, ideally Germany or UKNice to haveSome people management and technical interviewing experienceDesigned a technical interview process from scratchPrevious experience at a fully remote companyInterview processWe want to see how you think, build, and lead — not test you on algorithms. Here's the process:30 min — Intro call with our talent team45 min — Interview with Grigory60 min — Technical interview1.5 hr — AI-assisted build session: system design for a real feature, then building part of it with AI2 hr — Leadership session with the foundersThen you’ll get the offer! If we don't make an offer, we'll tell you why.What Secfix gives youRemote: 100% remote with a real virtual office in GatherSalary: Competitive, benchmarked to European market rates (we'll share specifics once we talk)Equity: Generous package — we're all owners hereDevelopment budget: €1,000/year — yours to spend on whatever makes you betterWorkspace: Remote workspace support + co-working accessHolidays: 26 days + local public holidaysHealth insurance: Comprehensive coverageAnnual retreat: Last time we went to Alicante 🇪🇸 — before that, the Austrian Alps, Portugal, Italy, and the Spanish IslandsTech: MacBook, monitors, headphones — the latestFind more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow
